name: intl
summary: I added a tower pass (parts/tower.mjs), which build.mjs now runs after all the other parts. It rewrites every exposed face of plot 0's tower with 1-wide limestone piers and recessed strips of dark glass with gray_terracotta spandrels, adds floodlights along the foot of each tower wall, rebuilds the Atlas sphere as open rings 11 across with a tilted axis, and turns the tower's remaining cut/chiseled sandstone into smooth_sandstone. The wings, gardens, the plot 1 and 2 buildings, every footprint and every height are untouched. Check: 0 floating blocks, 0 unsupported attachments, 25 orphans (v1 had 32; none are in the cells I changed). All new blocks exist in 1.21.1.

revisions.comment:
The low Fifth Avenue wings, the roof gardens and the two Channel Gardens buildings read well: keep them, every plot, footprint and height exactly. Plot 0's TOWER does not:
1. The tower's big faces are blank sandstone walls (only the edge columns have windows). Every face of the International Building tower, all four sides from the wing roofs to the crown, must carry the Rockefeller Center fluting top to bottom: continuous 1-wide limestone piers proud of the wall, alternating with 1-wide recessed dark window strips (gray/black stained glass panes, gray_terracotta spandrels every storey, about 1 window in 5 lit warm), exactly like 30 Rock and like the wings below it. No blank wall areas anywhere on the tower.
2. Its setbacks should read as clean tiers: each setback ledge capped with a slab/stair coping and a low parapet, floodlit from the ledge (light blocks hidden in it) so the upper faces glow at dusk; the crown a flat roof with a low penthouse.
3. ATLAS must be unmistakable from above and from Fifth Avenue: in the forecourt on Fifth Avenue (east, high x) on the entrance axis, a big bronze figure (copper / exposed and weathered copper / brown terracotta, about 12 tall incl. a granite plinth of polished andesite 3 tall) bending under a large open ARMILLARY SPHERE about 11 across made of thin rings (copper blocks / cut copper / waxed weathered copper, chains), with a tilted axis through it; floodlit from the forecourt paving so it stands out against the dark entrance behind it. The forecourt opens fully to the Fifth Avenue sidewalk.
4. Use one consistent limestone: the same block as the wings.

applied: 1. Fluting: every exposed face of the tower, all four sides, now has 1-wide smooth_sandstone piers flush with the face, alternating with 1-wide strips set back one block. The faces run from the ledge or wing roof below up to the crown band on the main tower, or to the parapet band on the lower steps. The strips have gray_stained_glass_pane windows with a gray_terracotta spandrel every storey. Behind each window is ochre_froglight (lit, about 1 in 5, chosen by a hash per window) or gray_concrete (dark). Corners stay solid piers. That is 6,551 strip cells, and the renders of all four sides show no blank wall left between the wing roofs and the crown band.

2. Tiers: every setback ledge (y 58, 104, 131, and 141 at the foot of the penthouse) keeps its edge parapet and smooth_sandstone_slab coping. Each now has a solid limestone base course where the ledge meets the wall above, and an ochre_froglight set flush in the deck every 3 cells along the foot of that wall (72 lights) to light the faces above. The crown stays a flat roof with the low penthouse.

3. Atlas: I cleared the old dense rings, which read as a solid copper blob from Fifth Avenue, and redrew the sphere as thin open rings centred on (67,16,27.5). There is a meridian 11 across facing Fifth Avenue, an equator, a second meridian, a tilted ecliptic band in waxed_exposed_copper, and a tilted axis through the centre with lightning_rod ends. The bronze figure, the polished andesite plinth, the granite pylons and the paving uplights stay. Nothing is built in the strip between the forecourt and Fifth Avenue, so the forecourt is open to the sidewalk. Lanterns that had stood on the old rings, and one figure block they had held up, were removed; one lantern now stands on top of the sphere.

4. One limestone: the tower walls and piers are smooth_sandstone, the same block as the wings. All cut_sandstone and chiseled_sandstone on the tower above the wings (quoins, crown pier heads) was changed to smooth_sandstone.
skipped: The ledge floodlights are flush in the deck, so they are visible from above rather than hidden. Hiding them under a cover would have meant raising the ledge decks.
The sphere is 11 across north–south and up–down, as asked, but only 9 east–west. The forecourt is only x 63..71 on the lot, and everything east of it is off the footprint.
The figure keeps its v1 height: a 4-course plinth and a body from y 6 to 15, about 14 blocks in all. I did not reshape it to the 3-tall plinth and roughly 12-tall total you described.
The penthouse and the crown band (y 139..142) have no windows, as the plan specifies for the crown.
